strengths: Hook is cinematic and immediately useful: last train, shutters, fluorescent konbini.
The article answers why hours exist, then what to do if a door is locked.
Scenarios and FAQ match first-time visitor questions without turning into a nightlife guide.
Sibling articles are scoped out early so this piece can stay on hours.

issues.location: Why Late Hours Fit Japanese Daily Life — Train-shaped days
issues.problem: Missed-last-train konbini is framed as food, warmth, ATM, and a bathroom in one box. Many urban stores have no customer toilet. A visitor who plans around that sentence can get stuck.
issues.suggestion: Keep food, warmth, and ATM. Hedge restrooms: only some stores have them; do not count on one.

issues.location: How Japanese People Use the Night Store + Real-Life Scenarios (3 a.m. parent)
issues.problem: Fever medicine and children’s medicine are presented as ordinary late-night konbini buys. OTC stock is limited and store-dependent; many shops have none. The scene teaches the wrong errand.
issues.suggestion: Use a reliable night buy (drink, cooling sheet, diapers if stocked) or hedge: a thin OTC shelf at some stores, not a pharmacy.

issues.location: Late Does Not Mean Every Store — 2024/2026 figures paragraph
issues.problem: The press-stat paragraph is denser than the surrounding magazine prose and may cause a mid-section skim.
issues.suggestion: Keep the 7-Eleven hedge; shorten the 2024 clause so the visitor takeaway lands faster.

issues.problem: “Do not treat one locked door as the end of Japanese convenience” sounds like a slogan after otherwise practical advice.
issues.suggestion: End on the next-node instruction only.
